clue.text: New showing of The Sorcerer, unabridged

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the stretch of words that follows, so 'of' points inside them

explanation.surface: A theatre revives Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta The Sorcerer in its full, uncut version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points into 'Sorcerer, unabridged', whose letters ...RER UN... carry the answer across the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat broadcast or second screening of a show is a fresh airing of something already seen.

clue.text: A1 piano chords arranged, as in a Gershwin piece

indicators.note: musical arrangement doubles as rearranging the letters of the pieces before it

parts.note: A1 is A plus the figure 1 read as the letter I
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: First-class piano chords, arranged in the style of a Gershwin composition.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'Al' is an OCR slip for 'A1' (first-rate), which gives AI. With P and CHORDS that makes nine letters to rearrange. The Gershwin piece is Rhapsody in Blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Gershwin's best-known concert work is Rhapsody in Blue, so music styled like it is effusive and free-form in that manner.

clue.text: Ticking-off for salesperson on the tiles

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
roof tiles cover the top of a house, so on the tiles means up on the roof

explanation.surface: A sales rep gets scolded after a night out on the tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the tiles' is British slang for a wild night out, which is the surface's picture; here it literally means up on the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticking-off is British for a scolding, the same as a rebuke.

clue.text: Not a name on a railway line?

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A question whether a station or line has no name at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Nary is dialect for never a, used in phrases like 'nary a word'.

clue.text: Rush-stick, we hear, can deliver a great blow

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the words before are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: rush means hurry and a walking stick is a cane

explanation.surface: Someone wielding a stick in a hurry can land a heavy blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush-stick' spoken gives HURRY CANE, which sounds like the storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical cyclone is a very strong wind, a blow in the weather sense.

clue.text: Job given back in it, check bank-account

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
a bank statement is the printed account of transactions

explanation.surface: Someone is told their job is restored, but should check the bank account to be sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in it' acts as link words between the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being restored to a post one lost means being put back in employment.

clue.text: American composer leads in very early sonata

indicators.note: the leading letters of the following words are taken, the leads of each

explanation.surface: An American composer is credited as a pioneer of the very early sonata.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer.

clue.text: Banking flap-no lire exchanged after the first of April

indicators.note: the rearranged pieces come after the April letter
only the opening letter of April is wanted
currency exchange suggests swapping the letters around

explanation.surface: Some currency trouble on April Fool's Day: no lire exchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' rearranges NO LIRE into ILERON, placed 'after' A from April. The surface makes 'Banking' about money; it means an aircraft tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's hinged wing surface makes it roll, tilting the plane in a turn.

clue.text: Peggotty upset — got out of ancient land

indicators.note: being upset means jumbled, so the letters of the name are mixed up

explanation.surface: Peggotty, the Dickens character, is upset at being thrown out of an old country.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters GOT 'out of' PEGGOTTY, leaving PEGTY, and 'upset' them. Peggotty is the nurse in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: The country of the pharaohs is one of the oldest civilisations.

clue.text: Recycled paper in a long dress

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for long, as on clothing sizes

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A long gown made from recycled paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recycled' turns PAPER into PPARE, which goes 'in' A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing in general is one's garb or attire.

clue.text: Rout-so equalize endlessly, in showy French style

indicators.note: a showy display rearranges things for effect, so the letters are put in a new order
the last letter of the word equalize is dropped

explanation.surface: A rout is equalised in a flamboyant French manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the final E from EQUALIZE, and 'showy' rearranges ROUTSO plus EQUALIZ.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornate decorative manner of Louis XIV's reign is a named period style of furniture and design.

clue.text: In a perfect world, allied members re-assemble with young leader

indicators.note: members coming back together in a new order means the letters are rearranged
only the first letter of young is wanted, its leader

explanation.surface: Ideally the allies would regroup with a youthful commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members re-assemble' rearranges ALLIED to IDEALL, and Y is the 'leader' of young.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means under the best conditions, as things would be if everything were as hoped.

clue.text: Where to buy peach?

definitions.meaning: slang for informing on someone to the authorities

explanation.definitionFit: A store sells goods; to grass someone up is to inform, an old sense of peach.

clue.text: Fashion for men announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken, so the word is said rather than spelt

parts.note: guys are men

explanation.surface: A men's fashion line is announced.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashion can mean a manner or outward form, as in 'in the guise of'.

clue.text: Pen a bit short for this legal document

indicators.note: the word falls slightly short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to pen is to write

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to pen a brief legal paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A court order or summons is a formal written legal instrument.

clue.text: Burn British castle

parts.note: in chess the rook is also called the castle

explanation.surface: A British castle burns down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' is a Scottish word for a stream, not fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A burn is a small stream in Scotland, the same as a creek.

clue.text: Wanton maid's gold sovereign?

indicators.note: wanton means unruly, so the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: the word maid's with its s

explanation.surface: A loose maid's gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A gold sovereign is a British coin; here it is a king who turned things to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek myth's Phrygian king turned everything he touched to gold, a gold-making monarch.

clue.text: Getting rid of Sherwood? (Arden too, if set badly!)

indicators.note: something set badly is out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Felling Sherwood Forest, with the Forest of Arden too if the plan goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Sherwood and Arden are both English forests.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing a forest such as Sherwood means removing its trees.

clue.text: Ship-breaker

definitions.meaning: one who wrecks or smashes things

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a fast warship and anyone who wrecks things.

clue.text: Round potato for example in skips, showing bumps

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for skips

parts.note: prances means skips about
O is round in shape
a potato is a tuber

explanation.surface: A round potato in a skip shows lumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OTUBER inside PRANCES, after PR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumps sticking out from a surface are swellings or projections.

clue.text: Indicate left terminal

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a terminal is an end

explanation.surface: A sign points to the terminal on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow is to signal what is coming.

clue.text: How French a remark!

explanation.definitionFit: It is the French for how and also an English word for an observation.

clue.text: Inter-city? No, town!

definitions.meaning: to inter is to put in the ground
a Lancashire town in north-west England

explanation.walkthrough: Inter-city looks like a train; split, Inter is a verb and the place is a town, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to entomb; it is also a town near Manchester.

clue.text: Booms can produce such pals

indicators.note: the letters given can produce a new word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Loud booms can make close friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Very close friends are called bosom pals, the word describing intimacy.

clue.text: Perfect state

definitions.meaning: complete, as in a perfect stranger

explanation.definitionFit: Absolute, as in a perfect fool, and to speak or say.

clue.text: Nothing to spoil this Persian poet

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to mar is to spoil

explanation.surface: Nothing could spoil this Persian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Khayyam, the Persian author of the Rubaiyat, is known by this first name.

clue.text: Put out this battered item

indicators.note: something battered is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Throw away this damaged item.
explanation.definitionFit: To give off or discharge is to send out.

clue.text: Penny on farm butter is a swindle!

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: a ram butts, so is a butter on the farm

explanation.surface: Paying a penny for butter on the farm is a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one that butts, a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is British slang for a racket or fraud.

clue.text: Vessel in which English master is at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship on which an English captain is out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is at sea' shuffles E with MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat driven by steam is a vessel.

clue.text: Disaster of attempt to include the superannuated

indicators.note: one word is to include the other inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
superannuated people are old, the aged

explanation.surface: An attempt to include pensioners ends in disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe or calamity is a disaster.

clue.text: Currently, place not recommended for extremists

definitions.text: Currently, place not recommended for extremists

parts.words: Currently, place not recommended for extremists
parts.note: a spot in the middle of a current, the very place people of extreme views avoid

explanation.definitionFit: It is the middle of a river's flow, a central position extremists shun.

clue.text: Man as safe as a rock?

definitions.meaning: slang for a strongbox, as used by safe-crackers
the apostle's name means rock in Greek

explanation.definitionFit: It is a boy's name, criminal slang for a strongbox, and the Greek-derived name meaning stone.
